source.title: SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation
source.authors: Ming-Jie Li; Wai-Man Si; Michael Backes; Yang Zhang; Yi-Sen Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests benign fine-tuning effects on harmful-response rates and evaluates a jailbreak suffix, using behavioral rates rather than the original studies' methods or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for benign Alpaca and commonsense-15k fine-tuning, and for MultiGCG suffixes. Its linear-probe results concern safety-related representations, but do not test whether safety is localized in a few weights or ranks, nor the first-token KL claim.
record.test_reason: Benign Alpaca and commonsense-15k LoRA, DoRA and PiSSA fine-tuning of four safety-tuned chat or instruct models, with Llama-Guard harmful rates before and after. This directly tests V2 with a PEFT recipe, not the originals' full setup. The MultiGCG experiment compares fine-tuning and defence methods under attack with no readable values, so it gives no usable V4 result.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that benign LoRA-style fine-tuning (LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA) compromises safety alignment. They attribute this to changes in safety features, shown by probe accuracy drops and a gradient-overlap proposition. Their SaLoRA, a fixed safety-subspace projection plus task-specific initialization, preserves alignment, including under MultiGCG, with comparable or better commonsense utility.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign Alpaca/commonsense fine-tuning and measures harmful-response rates after training, but does not reproduce the original studies' complete methods; it also evaluates a MultiGCG suffix and proposes SaLoRA.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported harmful rates vary by model, adapter method, rank, and dataset. The commonsense-15k table gives no pre-fine-tuning harmful-rate baseline. The MultiGCG outcomes are figure-only in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes trained on original Llama-2-chat-7B safety features lose over 10% accuracy at each layer after LoRA fine-tuning. SaLoRA fine-tuned models keep probe accuracy similar to the original.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign LoRA fine-tuning shifts probe-readable safety representations; constraining updates orthogonal to them preserves them.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting adapter updates orthogonal to the top singular directions of harmful-prompt features (SaLoRA) keeps harmful rate near the pre-fine-tuning level (1.4–4.4% on Llama models). It lowers Mistral's harmful rate below baseline (31.7–36.5% vs 47.8%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erosion can be largely prevented by freezing a low-rank safety-feature subspace during PEFT.

record.problems: The harmful-rate evaluation uses the 30% AdvBench test subset and Llama-Guard-3-8B; uncertainty estimates or repeated-run variation are not reported. MultiGCG results are only shown in a figure and lack exact values in the text. The commonsense-15k harmful rates have no pre-fine-tuning baseline.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 post-hoc combinations (Self-Reminder, InferAligner, Vaccine, and Safe LoRA) were omitted because the catalog focuses on the benign fine-tuning effect and they are additional post-hoc interventions. Table 2 commonsense-task accuracies and Figure 6 initialization comparisons were omitted because they measure utility or initialization performance rather than harmful compliance.

untested.parts: Full-parameter fine-tuning, varying example counts or epochs, carefully selected benign subsets, and closed models are not tested. Only 1-epoch PEFT on Alpaca and commonsense-15k.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling or decoding attacks. The MultiGCG suffix is evaluated without a readable rate or an un-attacked original-model comparison.
A low-rank safety subspace is assumed in method design, not tested as a localization finding.
The proposition argues benign gradients overlap safety weight regions. This concerns why fine-tuning erodes safety, not why alignment is token-shallow; no test.
No training that deepens safety across response positions.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's SaLoRA-based limits_scope and challenges labels on V2 are removed: SaLoRA is the authors' mitigation, not a benign-fine-tuning condition. Likewise the V4 'absent' label on SaLoRA under MultiGCG is removed. Table 1 values were checked against the flattened table and match. Mistral starts at 47.8% harmful, so its rises are from an already weak baseline. Single runs, no uncertainty reported; Llama-Guard-3-8B is the judge on a 30% AdvBench subset.

versions.untested_parts: Tests Alpaca and commonsense-15k fine-tuning, but not carefully selected benign-data strategies generally or a range of fine-tuning example counts.
Tests MultiGCG suffixes only; does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Discusses benign-data gradients perturbing safety-related weight regions, but does not test why safety behavior is shallow.
SaLoRA projects adapter updates relative to safety features; it does not train safety to extend across response positions or test whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.display_finding: The harmful rate rose from 0% to 13.8–35.7% on Llama-2, from 1.4% to 8.7–14.5% on Llama-3.1, and from 47.8% to 64.5–86.9% on Mistral.
